image_description: A grey whale breaching or surfacing in blue ocean water. The head and rostrum are visible emerging from the water, showing mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. A pectoral flipper is visible on the left side. Water spray surrounds the emerging body parts. A watermark '© Roi Hlaker' is overlaid across the center of the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is partially submerged and viewed from a low angle; the top of the rostrum where blowholes would be located is obscured by water spray and viewing angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible skin on the emerging head shows characteristic mottled grey coloration with distinct white/light patches consistent with barnacle colonies.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The posterior back and dorsal region are completely submerged or outside the frame; only the anterior head/shoulder region is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and one flipper are visible; the full body shape cannot be assessed due to submersion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with Head_and_Face checkpoint; visible skin exhibits correct mottling and barnacle patterns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or submerged; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Left pectoral flipper is visible emerging from water; appears broad and paddle-shaped consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail flukes are completely submerged and not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible skin surface shows rough texture with raised areas consistent with callosities and barnacle attachments.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Watermark text '© Roi Hlaker' shows slight character irregularity and edge softness typical of AI-generated or processed text overlays, but remains legible. Not a structural defect of the subject.

Water droplets and spray exhibit slightly uniform, painterly texture rather than crisp individual droplets; edges blend softly into background suggesting minor generation artifact in fluid dynamics simulation.
Edge definition between the pectoral flipper and surrounding water is slightly soft with minor haloing, indicating possible boundary blending issues common in AI-generated aquatic scenes.
